key_insight: Train high-fidelity human appearance with image generation first, then use that learned appearance as a prior to drive controllable video synthesis—decoupling appearance modeling from temporal and camera modeling to boost quality and control.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of jointly modeling human appearance, motion, and camera viewpoint from limited multi-view data, avoiding the trade-off between controllability and visual fidelity found in prior methods.
method: Image-first learning: train a high-quality human appearance model on still images to capture fine-grained texture and identity.
Appearance-as-prior video synthesis: condition a temporal generation module on the learned image prior while separately modeling motion and camera to preserve appearance across frames.
Controllable conditioning and data-efficient training: use pose/camera controls and a training scheme designed to work with sparse multi-view data.
impact: Enables practitioners to generate more realistic, identity-preserving, and controllable human videos (for animation, virtual avatars, VFX) while reducing dependence on large multi-view datasets and improving modularity of generation components.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: two-stage flow showing 'Image-first appearance learning' -> 'Appearance prior' -> 'Controllable video synthesis (motion + camera)'
Before vs After comparison: side-by-side frames highlighting improved texture/identity preservation and temporal consistency
Control grid: matrix showing same identity under varying poses and camera viewpoints to illustrate controllability
Data-efficiency chart: performance (quality/control) vs amount of multi-view data comparing ReImagine to baselines
paper_title: ReImagine: Rethinking Controllable High-Quality Human Video Generation via Image-First Synthesis
paper_authors: Zhengwentai Sun, Keru Zheng, Chenghong Li, Hongjie Liao, Xihe Yang
